subject: Under-stairs storage designed to fit
hook: Before anyone designs your under-stairs cupboard, check these five things.
ig:
Before anyone designs your under-stairs cupboard, check these five things.

Under-stairs storage is the most awkward space in most houses, which is exactly why it is worth planning properly. A generic unit leaves a dead triangle at the back. A unit designed to fit uses the slope.

1. Measure the slope, not just the box. Tallest height, shortest height and depth back to the wall.
2. Find the services. Meters, consumer units and broadband boxes need to stay reachable.
3. Check the floor and stringer. Neither is usually straight, and that is fine if your maker scribes the panels to suit.
4. List what will live there. Coats need hanging height, shoes suit shallow pull-outs, a hoover needs a tall bay.
5. Look at the hallway. Radiators and door swings decide between pull-outs and hinged doors.

Get those five right and the rest of the design follows. Bespoke under-stairs storage starts with a good survey, and we do that as part of a free, no-obligation consultation.

Save this for when you measure up, and tap the link in bio to see what we build.
fb:
Most houses we visit have the same story under the stairs: a door, a dark cupboard, and a pile of shoes and bags nobody can reach past.

With guests on the way over the next few weeks, it is the space most people wish worked harder. Before you plan anything, check five things: the slope (tallest and shortest heights, plus depth), where the meter and cables are, how level the floor and stringer are, what you actually want to store, and how much room the hallway gives for doors or pull-outs.

Swipe through for what each one means. If you would like a second pair of eyes, our free design consultation covers all of it, followed by an itemised quote.
